Retrieval-Augmented Generation FAQ

What is RAG?

Retrieval-augmented generation is a technique that combines a vector index with a large language model.

How does RAG improve answer quality?

It grounds the model output in retrieved documents instead of relying on parametric memory alone.

When should you use RAG?

Use RAG when you need answers tied to a specific, updatable corpus.

Why not use fine-tuning instead?

Fine-tuning bakes knowledge into the weights and is harder to update.
